newsitem.title: USA: NASDAQ market makers should offer liquidity - group.
newsitem.headline: NASDAQ market makers should offer liquidity - group.

text.p: Nasdaq market makers should be required to provide minimum liquidity levels for mature stocks, or risk losing their privileges, the Electronic Traders Association said in a paper released on Friday.
The group's paper expands on an argument it outlined in a letter to the Securities and Exchange Commission last week.

The group, which represents order-entry firms and related companies, wants the market makers to publish and honor their price quotes in 1,000 share increments rather than the minimum size required by a pilot program.
"If they call themselves a market maker they should be required to make a market," said Richard Roberts, a former SEC commissioner and an attorney representing the association.

In the paper, the group argued that unless market makers provide adequate liquidity "there is no justification for allowing these firms extraordinary benefits." Those benefits include 1/8-point subsidies, short sale exemptions and favorable net capital and leverage rules, the group said.
